question: Should Crabbox land the safe first slice now—detect unsupported Jujutsu workspaces, explain the colocated-Git path, and document it—while deferring native Jujutsu revision adaptation until a minimized reproduction is available?
rationale: The current maintainer comment establishes a preferred first slice but the permanent interoperability contract is still a product and compatibility choice; source evidence alone cannot decide whether native revision semantics should become part of the core sync contract.

options.title: Land safe detection first
options.body: Reject unsupported Jujutsu workspace layouts with actionable colocated-Git guidance and document the supported path while collecting a minimized native-adapter reproduction.

options.title: Sponsor native adaptation
options.body: Define and implement a Jujutsu revision-to-manifest contract after the reporter supplies a minimized multi-parent workspace and expected remote-tree result.

options.title: Support colocated Git only
options.body: Document colocated Git as the permanent supported workflow and do not add native Jujutsu revision semantics to Crabbox core.

recommendation.title: Land safe detection first
recommendation.body: Reject unsupported Jujutsu workspace layouts with actionable colocated-Git guidance and document the supported path while collecting a minimized native-adapter reproduction.

likelyOwner.reason: This person supplied the latest item-specific scope guidance and is the strongest available routing signal for the interoperability decision.
